Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

Please solve this issue: Retrieving time to refit the estimator in BaseSearchCV
Basically, I'm trying to figure out how much time it takes to refit the best model on the full data after doing grid/random search. What I can so far do is retrieve the time it takes to fit and score each model:
```
import sklearn.datasets
import sklearn.model_selection
import sklearn.ensemble

X, y = sklearn.datasets.load_iris(return_X_y=True)

rs = sklearn.model_selection.GridSearchCV(
    estimator=sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier(),
    param_grid={'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}
)
rs.fit(X, y)
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'])
print(rs.cv_results_['mean_score_time'])
```
In case I run this on a single core, I could time the whole search procedure and subtract the time it took to fit the single folds during hyperparameter optimization. Nevertheless, this isn't possible any more when setting `n_jobs != 1`.

Thus, it would be great to have an attribute `refit_time_` which is simply the time it took to refit the best model.

Usecase: for [OpenML.org](https://openml.org) we want to support uploading the results of hyperparameter optimization, including the time it takes to do the hyperparameter optimization.

# 1. GridSearchCV, n_jobs=2 (parallel CV), single metric

      "refit_time_ is a positive float (%r)" % gs.refit_time_)

      "refit_time_ is smaller than total CV fit time")

# 2. RandomizedSearchCV, single metric
rs = RandomizedSearchCV(est, {'n_estimators': [2, 3, 4, 5]}, n_iter=2,
                        random_state=0)
rs.fit(X, y)
check(hasattr(rs, 'refit_time_') and rs.refit_time_ > 0,
      "RandomizedSearchCV sets refit_time_")

# 3. Multi-metric with refit set to a scorer name

                     scoring=['accuracy', 'f1'], refit='accuracy', cv=3)
gs_mm.fit(X, y)
check(hasattr(gs_mm, 'refit_time_') and gs_mm.refit_time_ > 0,
      "multi-metric GridSearchCV with refit='accuracy' sets refit_time_")

# 4. refit=False -> attribute must be absent for both classes
for cls, kwargs in ((GridSearchCV, {'param_grid': {'n_estimators': [2, 3]}}),
                    (RandomizedSearchCV,

                      'n_iter': 2})):
    s = cls(est, refit=False, cv=3, random_state=0, **kwargs)
    s.fit(X, y)

# 5. refit=False still exposes best_params_/best_index_ as before

      "best_params_/best_index_ unaffected")

# 6. estimator without y (unsupervised path) still works
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
gs_u = GridSearchCV(PCA(), {'n_components': [2, 3]}, cv=3)
gs_u.fit(X)
check(hasattr(gs_u, 'refit_time_') and gs_u.refit_time_ > 0,
      "unsupervised GridSearchCV (fit without y) sets refit_time_")

print("\nALL EDGE CASE CHECKS PASSED")
